key_insight: Enforcing symmetry between two grain boundaries in a periodic cell enables diffusion-based generation of structures conditioned on a well-defined grain-boundary energy.
engineering_relevance: This approach could make grain-boundary structure an inverse-design variable for engineering polycrystalline materials.
method: Extend MatterGen with a symmetry projection at every denoising step.
Generate atoms near one boundary and reconstruct the equivalent partner by symmetry.
Condition Al Σ5(210)[001] boundary generation on energy from a machine-learning interatomic potential.
evidence_signal: All 350 generated structures retained equivalent boundary pairs after relaxation; for three well-supported, in-range energy targets, 44–70% landed within ±0.1 J/m², and 90 of 91 near-target structures were distinct from training structures under the adopted geometric criterion.
watch_item: Energy targeting weakened at higher energies and failed outside the training range; evaluation was limited to one Al grain-boundary type using an ML interatomic potential.
paper_title: Generating grain boundary structures at a specified energy with a symmetry-constrained diffusion model
